title: Independent reclosure of repaired Chronicles batch01 places_2
reviewer: independent reviewer of author repairs; no draft edits
methodJa: 全35件の現行草稿・sidecar SHAとprofile canonical SHAを現manifestに照合。4つの修正稿を固定WEB本文と現在のreader fields/facts/map-policyに再照合し、変化していない31件は既存独立レビューのdraft/evidence両SHAが現在バイトと一致する場合に限り前回の意味判定を保持した。既存のWikipedia実本文locatorはURL・対象・注記に変更がないものだけ再利用。

rows.priorReviewer: WEB 4:32 names a Simeonite town. The Ain article is a different/related Levitical allotment and does not prove this list-item’s archaeological identity; related-section link and null coordinates are appropriately restrained.

WEB 6:72–73 context assigns Anem among Issachar’s towns given to Gershom. The live article explicitly cites 1 Chronicles 6:73, notes the En-gannim identification debate, and says exact location is unknown; the profile preserves that uncertainty.

WEB 2:23 names Aram as an actor taking Jair’s towns but does not resolve region/polity versus Aramean people. The personal Aram in 1:17 is a namesake ancestor, correctly excluded. Related-only article, no map point.
WEB 5:6 and 5:26 use Assyria as the kings’ realm. The article distinguishes ancient state/empire and modern Assyrians; the regional map policy suppresses a misleading point.
WEB 1:46 directly says Hadad’s city was Avith. Live article explicitly identifies the Edomite city/capital and says its location is unknown; proposed south-Israel/Jordan sites remain tentative.

WEB 5:8 uses Baal-meon as a place in the Reubenite settlement range. The live article calls it a Reubenite town and presents Ma’in only as an identification by some; the profile does not repeat the unsupported Elisha-birth claim in that article.
WEB 13:6 itself equates Baalah with Kiriath-Jearim. Live article lists Ba’alah as a name and cites 1 Chronicles 13:6; competing site identifications are preserved, coordinates remain null.

WEB 5:11,12,16,23; 6:62,71 uses Bashan as a broad territory. Live article describes the ancient northern Transjordan region spanning present Jordan/Syria; regional point remains explicitly unverified.

WEB 4:21 says “house of Ashbea” amid Shelah genealogy and linen-working families; it does not establish a separate town. Current empty passages, no link, and suppressed map are appropriately cautious. Search for Beth-ashbea/Beth Ashbea/Ashbea found no fitting Wikipedia entry; external reference works also describe the place-versus-family ambiguity.

rows.primaryTextRecheck: 1CH 6:68 “Jokmeam with its pasture lands, Beth Horon with its pasture lands,” and 7:24 “built Beth Horon the lower and the upper…”; pinned witness inventory/targets/chronicles1-web-verses.json SHA 04e30515896ff7d50f0fcef3a1bafd1984d232b9bce84644cab641bc4d1d634a.
rows.currentFieldAssessmentJa: Fixed WEB 1CH 6:68 names Beth Horon among towns assigned to Levites; the current passages include 6:68 and 7:24, and the introductory wording is limited to the earlier town-name/ pasture-land listing. 7:24 remains a gated fact about Sheerah building Upper and Lower Beth Horon. Coordinate is null and map pin suppressed because the profile combines two towns. The existing Bethoron article locator (lead and Hebrew Bible, lines 123–127) supports the biblical place; current note does not expose the later twin-town detail.
rows.wikipediaRecheck: Bethoron; lead and Hebrew Bible, lines 123–127; article says ancient Bethoron and names both towns; existing read timestamp 2026-10-16T04:40:06Z; relation unchanged.

rows.priorReviewer: WEB 6:59 names a Levitical town but does not identify which Beth Shemesh. Live article lists Judah, Naphtali, Issachar, and Egyptian namesakes and does not resolve this one; related-only link and uncertainty note are proper.
rows.priorActualArticleLocator: lead and disambiguation list; article body lines 105–114

rows.priorReviewer: WEB 6:78 explicitly locates Bezer east of Jordan in Reuben’s allotment. Live article identifies the Levitical/refuge city and says its site cannot be located with certainty; null coordinates and candidate-only policy are appropriate.

WEB 1:44 identifies Zerah as “of Bozrah” in the Edomite king list. Bozrah URL redirects to modern Busaira; its text says some researchers identify the biblical city with a site there, while displayed coordinates are the modern town. Related-only link and candidate-only map policy avoid treating modern coordinates as verified ancient coordinates.
WEB 11:37 calls Hezro a Carmelite, a place-origin demonym. Article is the biblical settlement, not Mount Carmel or the newer settlement; current scope and null coordinates respect that distinction.

WEB 6:72 lists Daberath among Issachar’s Levitical towns. Live article describes the Levitical town near Zebulun and says the modern Daburiyya survival is likely, not certain; candidate-only placement is restrained.

WEB 1:43 calls Dinhabah Bela’s city. Live article says it may correspond to Dibdiba, while noting unrelated Danaba/Danabe names elsewhere. Current text marks the location as tentative; no verified point.

The three cited contexts refer to people/half-tribe and their territory, not a standalone place-name. Empty place passages and map suppression correctly prevent a group card from becoming a geographic pin; retain as an explicitly rejected place candidate.

WEB 1:43, 18:11, 18:13 supports Edom as region/realm; 1:51 and 1:54 refer to chiefs/people and are correctly excluded. Article defines a historical kingdom across parts of modern Israel/Jordan/West Bank; no single point is asserted.

WEB 17:21 uses Egypt as a land/country. WEB 13:5 only contains “River of Egypt” as a river-boundary phrase, properly excluded from the country profile. Article is a country/state overview; coordinates stay null.
rows.priorActualArticleLocator: history of ancient Egypt and geography, article lines 160 onward

rows.priorReviewer: WEB 4:32 lists Etam among Simeonite towns; the Etam article’s main town relates to different biblical contexts (not this town). The current related-only link expressly limits its scope and no location is asserted.

WEB 5:9 and 18:3 explicitly name the Euphrates. WEB 1:48 only says “the River,” and 19:16 “beyond the River”; both are appropriately excluded from a direct named-mention profile. A river-wide single-point map is suppressed.

WEB 5:11 speaks of “sons of Gad,” a people/tribal group, not a place. The place candidate is excluded from passages and map pins; a place-only assignment must remain qualified/rejected, not recast as a geographic entity.

rows.primaryTextRecheck: 1CH 4:39 “They went to the entrance of Gedor…to seek pasture for their flocks.” 1CH 12:7 “…the sons of Jeroham of Gedor.” Pinned witness hash 04e30515896ff7d50f0fcef3a1bafd1984d232b9bce84644cab641bc4d1d634a; current evidence records both verse texts, neighboring context, exact URLs and text hashes.
rows.currentFieldAssessmentJa: The fixed WEB at 1CH 4:39 says “the entrance of Gedor” in the Simeonite pasture search; 12:7 says “the sons of Jeroham of Gedor.” The current evidence adjudicates 4:39 as a place-name mention but does not merge it into the 12:7 town profile. The reader note explicitly says the text does not establish that the two refer to the same site. This is a sound conservative treatment; exact geographic identity remains unresolved and no map pin is displayed.
rows.wikipediaRecheck: No fitting dedicated Wikipedia article; current author evidence records English Gedor/biblical place searches and checks the minor places list. This stays a documented no-fit, not an assumed match.

rows.priorReviewer: WEB 2:23 has Geshur as a polity/territorial actor; 3:2 has a king of Geshur, a related political territory. Live article describes the ancient Levant territory and its uncertain extent. Keep the realm/territory uncertainty and do not equate it with a single city point.

WEB 2:22, 5:9,10,16, 6:80, 26:31, 27:21 supports geographic Gilead. Crucially 2:23’s “father of Gilead” is a personal genealogical name, not included as regional use. Article defines a broad Transjordan region with no definite eastern boundary; null coordinates are suitable.

WEB 6:71 explicitly identifies Golan in Bashan as a Levitical city. Live article distinguishes ancient Golan city from the modern Golan Heights region and says the city site is not identified; map remains candidate-only.

WEB 5:26 names Halah as one deportation destination. Searches for “Halah,” “Halah biblical,” and “Halah Assyria” found no suitable Wikipedia place article (only unrelated results and a mention under Habor). Site remains unknown. The unverified candidate pin should not be treated as established.

WEB 6:76 identifies Hammon in Naphtali in the Levitical-town list. Live shared-section article distinguishes the Asher-border Hammon from the Naphtali Levitical city and cites 1 Chronicles 6:76; candidate pin is limited to this namesake.
rows.priorActualArticleLocator: H section, “Hammon”; list entry (opened page, lines around 830)

rows.priorReviewer: WEB 4:28 lists Hazarshual among Simeonite towns. Live shared-section article gives the Simeon–Judah border location and cites 1 Chronicles 4:28; exact site remains unknown and the candidate remains unverified.

rows.primaryTextRecheck: 1CH 3:1, 3:4, 6:55, 6:57, 11:1, 11:3, 12:23, 12:38, 29:27; excluded 26:31 on grammatical/kinship use (“Hebronites…according to their generations by fathers’ households”). Pinned witness SHA 04e30515896ff7d50f0fcef3a1bafd1984d232b9bce84644cab641bc4d1d634a.
rows.currentFieldAssessmentJa: The fixed WEB uses Hebron as the city in the retained passages. 1CH 26:31 “Hebronites” is a Levitical family/ancestral group, not the city, and is absent from the current profile passage list. The article and modern-location note distinguish the ancient city from the modern settlement; coordinate stays null.
rows.wikipediaRecheck: Hebron; article locator retained from prior read (article supports ancient city and current city distinction); note is not broadened beyond the evidence.

rows.priorReviewer: WEB 6:58 names Hilen as a Judah Levitical town. The live shared-section entry says Hilen/Hilez is an alternate name for the Judah Holon and separately lists the Moabite Holon; profile preserves site uncertainty.

rows.primaryTextRecheck: 1CH 10:11 “When all Jabesh Gilead heard all that the Philistines had done to Saul”; 10:12 gives the recovery/burial actions. Pinned witness SHA 04e30515896ff7d50f0fcef3a1bafd1984d232b9bce84644cab641bc4d1d634a.
rows.currentFieldAssessmentJa: At first-known 1CH 10:11, the town is named as the place whose inhabitants heard what happened to Saul. Current always-visible summary and role say only that. Recovery and burial of Saul and his sons are a separate fact gated at 10:12 with its own source. Coordinate remains null; modern location is qualified as multiple candidate sites.
rows.wikipediaRecheck: Jabesh-Gilead; lead and Identification, article body; article identifies an ancient Gilead town, mentions 1 Chronicles 10:11–12 and notes multiple proposed sites; existing read timestamp 2026-10-16T04:40:06Z.

rows.priorReviewer: WEB 6:78 places Jahzah east of Jordan in Reuben’s Levitical-town list. The live shared-section article identifies Jahaz/Jahaza/Jahazah/Jahzah as spelling variants and reports competing site locations; null coordinates/candidate-only pin are suitable.

WEB 6:78 uses Jericho as a locational landmark and 19:5 as the town where David tells the messengers to stay. The live article distinguishes present city from Tell es-Sultan/Old Jericho remains; the profile does not claim the modern city area is the ancient site.

All listed 24 occurrences name or clearly locate Jerusalem as the city, including the 3:4 base. The live article treats the ancient and modern city across an evolving urban area; the profile avoids treating present city limits as ancient boundaries.
